title: Existence of a fine log structure inducing labelled etale descent data
statement: Let T be a locally Noetherian scheme, U_a -> T a jointly surjective family of small etale objects, and D a FineLogEtaleDescentDatum: fine log structures on the U_a with natural multiplicative structure-preserving transition isomorphisms, diagonal identities and triple cocycle, evaluated on every common etale test object. There exists a fine log structure M on T and a labelled gluing e of M inducing exactly D. For this same M, if every local log structure of D is fine saturated, then M is fine saturated. No uniqueness or morphism gluing is asserted.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, p. 69; Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.8, pp. 107--108; Stacks sites.tex, Tags 04TR and 04TQ. Existence only: steps 1--4 of lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent.

proof.text: Use the small representatives of the sites in [def-weil-size-convention], in a universe also containing the covering index set and the section sets and products used in descent. Put $\mathcal C=T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and take its terminal object $T\to T$. The given family covers that object, and fibre products exist in $\mathcal C$, by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], $\mathcal C/T_a$ is the small etale site of $T_a$, and likewise on all overlaps. Thus the given $M_a$ and their transitions are sheaves and maps on the slice sites required for descent. Under these equivalences the structure sheaves agree: on an object $W\to T_a$ both assign $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, with the same restrictions. Relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives the same identifications on repeated slices; the slice over the terminal object is $\mathcal C$ itself.

source.place: Section 00XZ, section-localize; Definition 00Y0, definition-localize; Lemma 03EH, lemma-relocalize; specialization to the small etale sites

proof.text: Forget the monoid operations for the moment. Apply the existence clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the underlying set sheaves of $M_a$ and their given transition isomorphisms $\phi_{ab}$. The assumed cocycle is exactly its cocycle, including repeated indices. Obtain a sheaf of sets $M$ and isomorphisms $e_a:M|_{T_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_a$ with $e_b=\phi_{ab}e_a$ on every double overlap. These identifications induce the specified descent datum, rather than only isomorphic unlabelled local objects.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, with the gluing datum immediately preceding it

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-sheaf-structure-gluing] to this set sheaf $M$, its labelled $e_a$, the given monoid sheaves $M_a$, and $R=(\mathcal O_T,\cdot)$. The transitions preserve products, identity and the maps to $R$ by hypothesis. It supplies the monoid operations and $\alpha:M\to\mathcal O_T$ with every $e_a$ an isomorphism over $\mathcal O_T$.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps; sectionwise gluing of multiplication, unit, equations and the map to a fixed monoid sheaf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-condition-fine-chart-locality] to $(M,\alpha)$: its restrictions are log structures because $e_a$ identifies them over $\mathcal O_{T_a}$ with $M_a$. Transport each chosen fine chart through $e_a^{-1}$. The lemma verifies the log-unit axiom and makes the composite covering and these charts into fine charts for $M$. If the given chart monoids are saturated, its saturated conclusion makes $M$ fs.

lean.statement:
theorem fineLogEtaleDescent_exists
    {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian T] {ι : Type v} (U : ι → T.Etale)
    (hcover : ∀ x : T, ∃ (a : ι) (y : (U a).left), (U a).hom y = x)
    (D : FineLogEtaleDescentDatum U) :
    ∃ (M : EtaleLogStructure T) (_hM : M.IsFine) (e : D.Gluing M),
      (∀ a : ι, (D.localLog a).IsFineSaturated) → M.IsFineSaturated
